findings.summary: The pinned snapshot at tests/test_brief_prompt.py:295-306 does not describe the prompt the node ships. The snapshot reads 'Write a fragment only in one of the landing line's two exceptions - a negative result, ...' and places 'Nothing splices a fragment into the plan's landed record' before the small-node rule, while reckon/crew/prompts.py:197 emits 'Write a fragment only in one of the two cases it is for - you have a negative result, ...' and places that sentence after SMALL_NODE_RULE at :205-206. Both mismatches were introduced by 4f6c88c291, which hand-edited the snapshot instead of composing it, and they are visible in the run's own gate log (logs/head-arm-final2-1319294.log:16-31). The 'verbatim' pin therefore cannot guard the clause it exists to guard, and a reader of the snapshot is shown wording the product never emits.

The paragraph says the contract is one 'the prompt embeds verbatim' and then quotes a clause the prompt does not carry: the quote gives 'write one only when you have a negative result or a mechanism that does not fit a landing line, the landing line being then the node's whole prose account', while reckon/crew/prompts.py:196-200 says 'A per-node evidence fragment is optional: it is not the record and a routine landing writes none, so the landing line is the whole prose account of the node. Write a fragment only in one of the two cases it is for'. The quotation marks also close after 'as follows.' and reopen at 'your plan section.' with no opening mark at :522, so the passage claims an accuracy it does not have and a coordinator reading it cannot tell which words are the contract's.

The quoted landing clause is a paraphrase presented as the workers' contract: it reads 'A per-node evidence fragment is optional: write one only when you have a negative result or a mechanism that does not fit a landing line, the landing line being then the node's whole prose account of the node, and place it as follows.', while reckon/crew/prompts.py:195-200 carries different wording for the same clause. The skill text a coordinator reads to verify a landing therefore quotes words a worker was never given.
